name: Polymeric membrane capture
applications: coal and gas power flue gas

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas passes over a CO2-selective polymer membrane. A pressure difference across the membrane, created by compressing the feed and/or applying vacuum on the permeate side, drives CO2 through faster than nitrogen. Multiple stages and recycle raise purity and capture rate; no chemicals or steam are needed.

process_steps.name: First membrane stage
equipment: membrane modules (spiral wound or hollow fibre)

process_steps.name: Second stage or liquefaction for purity
equipment: membrane modules or CO2 liquefaction unit

reference_plants.name: Wyoming Integrated Test Center large pilot, Dry Fork Station
reference_plants.status: under construction in Sept 2023, slated to operate in 2024

advantages: No chemicals, little water, no steam
limitations: Power for compression and vacuum rises steeply at low CO2 concentration
Not yet proven at commercial scale on flue gas

costs.metric: Cost of CO2 captured, MTR Polaris membrane process (FEED study potential)
costs.basis: Stated as potential to capture below the DOE capture cost target of $40/tonne CO2 from coal-fired flue gas; FEED design basis is 5,600 t/d (about 2.0 Mt/yr), 70% of the 400-MWe Dry Fork Station plant's CO2; dollar year not stated

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR FEED study entry (FE0031846), p. 115

costs.metric: Cost of CO2 captured, MTR hybrid membrane-absorption process
costs.basis: Hybrid of Polaris membrane recycle stage (enriching flue gas from about 13 to 20% CO2) with a 5 molal piperazine advanced flash stripper on coal flue gas; current R&D value $54/t, target $43/t; dollar year not stated

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR project entry, Table 3 Power Plant Carbon Capture Economics, p. 123

costs.basis: Design value $10/m2 for spiral-wound modules and $30/m2 for plate-and-frame modules; dollar year not stated

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR membrane process parameter Tables 1 and 2, pp. 117 and 121

costs.metric: Membrane module manufacturing and installation cost, projected at full commercialization
costs.basis: Projected cost of planar plate-and-frame module skids at full commercialization stage; dollar year not stated

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR project entry, p. 120

performance.basis: Commercial Polaris averages 1,000 GPU (about 10 times conventional gas separation membranes); lab-scale studies demonstrated 3,000 GPU; design tables list 1,000 GPU (spiral-wound) and 1,700 GPU (plate-and-frame) at 30 degC, mixed gas

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR entries, pp. 116-117 and Tables 1-2, pp. 117, 121

performance.basis: Module design tables list CO2/N2 selectivity 30 (mixed gas, 30 degC) for spiral-wound and plate-and-frame; the narrative cites an average CO2/N2 selectivity of 50

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR entries, pp. 116-117, Tables 1-2 pp. 117, 121

performance.metric: CO2 recovery of membrane capture system (module design value)
performance.basis: Design values: 90% recovery at >96% purity and 140 bar (spiral-wound configuration); 70% recovery at >96% purity and 150 bar (plate-and-frame configuration)

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR membrane process parameter Tables 1 and 2, pp. 117, 121

performance.metric: CO2 capture rate of multi-stage membrane process
performance.basis: Multi-stage design overcomes the pressure-ratio constraint of single-stage systems; FEED study design basis captures 70% of Dry Fork Station emissions; operation at about 70%+ capture without recycle noted as lower-cost option

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR entries, pp. 116, 119 and 115

performance.metric: CO2 capture rate with selective recycle to boiler, 1-MWe pilot
performance.basis: Integrated membrane-boiler test with B&W 0.6-MWe coal-fired research boiler; a modest boiler efficiency reduction of 1.8% was measured at 90% capture, showing the selective-recycle process is feasible

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR project entry, p. 119

performance.metric: CO2 purity of product from membrane process
performance.basis: First capture stage permeate about 55-60% CO2, enriched to >85% CO2 by the second membrane stage; FEED design adds a CO2 purification unit producing >99% CO2 at 150 bar

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR entries, pp. 116 and 119

performance.basis: Target module lifetime three years; in extended flue-gas testing (more than 13,000 hours) fouling was not significant; spiral-wound modules accumulated 11,000 hours without significant degradation

source.note: NETL Compendium of Carbon Capture Technology 2024, MTR entries, pp. 118, 122
